newsitem.title: USA: Clinton's gender gap solid at 18 points - survey.
newsitem.headline: Clinton's gender gap solid at 18 points - survey.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's lead in the polls is being bolstered by an 18-point gender gap, showing that women favour him far more than men do, the women's political organisation EMILY's List said on Friday.
The Democratic, pro-abortion rights group's survey of 700 women and 300 men showed that female voters support Clinton by a 22-point margin, while men favour Clinton by only 4 points.

EMILY's List, which supports women candidates and tracks women's voting patterns, said Clinton's gender gap advantage has not narrowed following the Republican and Democratic national conventions. Such a narrowing has been the norm in recent years.

In congressional races, the survey found, most women support a Democratic candidate in their own districts, but they are split on whether Congress should be controlled by the Democrats or the Republicans.
Clinton's strong lead in recent polls does not mean voters will stay home on election day, according to the survey, which found 75 percent of women say the campaign "makes me want to go vote."
